relationships.description: Scott identifies their understanding as the policy breached, in his interpretation, by Dulles’s conditional-surrender negotiations. This is an explicit diplomatic agreement, not a general ideological affiliation.

relationships.label: Political-action planning target
relationships.description: Scott says Moss was selected in November 1962 for the CIA Political Action Group as part of planning to remove Castro. The role does not by itself prove Moss executed an assassination attempt.

relationships.label: Planned removal through covert action
relationships.description: The article explicitly identifies planning to get rid of Castro; note 78 cites agency records and the Inspector General report on CIA–Mafia plots.

relationships.label: Reported friendship in the 1950s
relationships.description: Endnote 80 attributes to Larry Kolb a claim, said to have been corroborated by Khashoggi, of a 1950s friendship with John Kennedy. This is a secondary personal-account assertion, not independently verified membership or proof of institutional action.

relationships.label: Hamburg meeting and Iran proposal
relationships.description: Scott reports Copeland’s and Kolb’s accounts that Copeland met the Iranian arms dealer, then prepared an Iran-policy proposal. Copeland’s assertion that it was not about hostages or Contras remains distinguished from later outcomes.

relationships.label: Hamburg negotiations witnessed by Kolb
relationships.description: Kolb explicitly places himself with Ghorbanifar, Copeland, Khashoggi and Schwimmer at the 1985 meeting. This is an identified transaction meeting, not inferred shared-group membership.

relationships.label: Participant in Hamburg Iran-initiative meeting
relationships.description: Scott gives Kolb’s explicit participant list in the negotiations; neither a permanent partnership nor agency employment is inferred.

relationships.label: Swiss banking interlock described through Hartmann
relationships.description: Scott connects Rappaport’s banking business to BCCI through Hartmann’s BCCI board seat, Intermaritime vice-chairmanship and BCCI subsidiary role; no personal BCCI board seat for Rappaport is asserted.

relationships.label: Authorized 1948 Italian-election covert operation
relationships.description: Scott says Dulles persuaded Washington to authorize the operation through both the NSC and CIA; this is a decision pathway, not a claim that NSC owned the agency.

relationships.label: Reported holder of off-budget covert-operation funds
relationships.description: Scott places ECA among cooperative organizations in whose hands CIA left off-book funds. His wording describes an apparent general practice rather than a quantified transfer on a specified date.

relationships.label: Exchanged reports on Moss and Cellini allegations
relationships.description: The body reports that FBI had advised CIA about Moss’s mistress and her brother; endnote 79 also describes CIA notifying FBI in December 1960 of Julia Cellini’s account of her brothers. This is an explicit interagency information exchange about allegations, not proof those allegations were substantiated.

relationships.label: Resigned officer returning in joint Cairo advisory mission
relationships.description: Scott says Copeland resigned from CIA to join Booz Allen, then returned to Cairo in March 1953 in effectively a joint mission. Copeland’s later claims about off-record requests from friends at Langley remain distinct from documented formal employment.

relationships.label: Former director in Safari Club account
relationships.description: Scott’s quotations explicitly identify Helms as former DCI while describing his later Tehran role and attributed private-network cooperation. His former office does not independently verify all alleged Safari Club operations.

relationships.label: Agency head before leaving in January 1977
relationships.description: The Trento passage identifies Bush as head of CIA; the Phillips passage separately places his departure in January 1977 before his banking committee role. These explicit offices are distinguished from disputed BCCI financing or chairmanship claims.

profileUpdates.description: Scott’s endnote 44 identifies ICI through its chairman, Lord McGowan, the recipient of John Foster Dulles’s letter defending international business arrangements against political barriers. The correspondence establishes a specific personal and corporate contact, not common ownership between the law firm and ICI.

Scott’s note 80 cites Larry Kolb’s account of a 1950s friendship between John Kennedy and Khashoggi, reportedly corroborated by Khashoggi. The account remains a secondary personal claim; the separate Kennedy-assassination book titles in notes do not themselves establish affiliations.

Scott identifies Castro as the target of November 1962 CIA political-action planning for which Edward Moss was to be used. Endnote 78 points to CIA records and an Inspector General report; the passage does not establish that every named operative carried out an attempted assassination.

Scott identifies Stalin and his party among contingent causes of the Cold War and describes Roosevelt’s Yalta understanding with Stalin on unconditional surrender when criticizing Dulles’s 1945 negotiations. These are a source interpretation and an identified diplomatic commitment, not financial-organization memberships.

Scott identifies Greenspun as Schwimmer’s earlier partner in gun-running to the emerging Israeli state and the person who introduced Schwimmer to Khashoggi in Las Vegas. Note 107 cites Slater for collaboration involving Greenspun, Schwimmer and Lansky; Helliwell’s participation is only tentative.

Scott’s note 107 cites a collaboration involving Lansky, Schwimmer and Greenspun in Israeli gun-running. His name also appears as the title of a CIA security file in note 79; that filing reference alone does not establish personal operational control over Moss or the Cellinis.

Scott discusses Khashoggi’s access to Nixon, his banking contact with Rebozo and disputed campaign-payment stories. Note 26 additionally quotes an alleged 1960 bargain concerning transfer of the Japanese M-fund’s control; its quid-pro-quo is expressly alleged. The 2014 publication date is not used as the date of these historical contacts.

Marshall appears mainly in Marshall Plan labels, Jonathan Marshall’s citation or Andrew Gavin Marshall’s editor credit; this article does not supply a new specific personal office or transaction by General George Marshall.
George identifies Kennan, Bush or other given names, not Harold C. George.
The State is part of the article title, a general public-state expression or a citation; it does not identify the South African journal.

The note says Helliwell may have been part of Israeli gun-running; a firm collaboration edge is not justified by this tentative wording.
Notes 103 and 105 explicitly state no published evidence establishes his participation in Safari Club covert operations; no such membership is inferred.
An unidentified Castle Bank customer named Richard M. Nixon is not established as the president; proposed hidden Bridge Company ownership is speculative.
The London-bank wording has an ambiguous antecedent. Explicit First International Bancshares committee chairmanship is already captured; BCCI chairmanship is not established.
The text assigns Bridge Company ownership to individual Booz Allen personnel, not the corporate firm itself.

The J. Henry Schroder Banking Corporation occurs only in a photograph caption giving former Wall Street headquarters. This does not establish ownership, patronage or an operational relationship with Sullivan and Cromwell merely because both are shown.
JPMorgan Chase and Co is a modern group in a concentration study, not necessarily the same historical entity as J. P. Morgan and Company; mere list appearance establishes no affiliation.
Modern JPMorgan Chase is listed, but no historical Chase Manhattan ownership or personnel relation is supplied; no legal identity chain is inferred from the name.
The source gives title and surname only; no fuller biographical name or founding date of ICI is inserted from outside the PDF.
The sentence attaches Socony confusingly to Standard Oil of California. That label is not used as an alias or as grounds to merge California and New York companies.
The passage says America’s post-Watergate paralysis in the field of undercover activity. Field is a common noun, not Frederick Vanderbilt Field; no affiliation is established.
JCS appears only in the title of Amy Zegart’s cited book about the CIA, JCS and NSC; this citation does not establish a Joint Chiefs role in the specific Italian-election funding operation.

The generated abbreviation CIA is not an approved alias for the Committee to Investigate Assassinations. These passages explicitly concern the Central Intelligence Agency; no CTIA affiliation is established.
The reference is to the Italian Christian Democratic Party receiving alleged funds via a Vatican priest, not the United States Democratic Party.
FBI refers to the Federal Bureau of Investigation in reports about Moss and Cellini and failures to act on BCCI warnings, not the Federation of British Industries.

NSC on page 27 occurs in the title of Zegart’s cited book. The operational NSC–CIA authorization relationship is supported by page 4 and already captured; the bibliography supplies no additional affiliation.

summary: Independent source-wide reread of all 27 pages, including photographs, captions, bibliography and all 123 endnotes, checked against the complete 764-identity catalog after a further 38-identity delta review rather than only existing Scott profiles. Literal-name, alias and all-surname leads were identity-resolved in context. This pass identifies additional cross-source people, an ICI chairman/correspondent, the Free Europe committee, Japanese M-fund administration and named oil-company relationships omitted by the earlier profile-centered audit. Publisher names, place names, ambiguous people and mere mentions were rejected. Existing specific Scott edges are retained rather than duplicated. New records are limited to explicitly named institutional or personal counterparties needed for specific affiliations.

coverage.limits: A manual reread plus normalized text leads supports a source-wide review, not an assertion that every possible connection in every wording has been exhaustively extracted. The supplied article is an attributed secondary argument; notes contain contested claims and denials. Unnamed shipping firms, undisambiguated bank customers, unspecified agency contacts and tentative associations remain unmodeled. Organizational succession is limited to the lineages explicitly described; the article’s erroneous or confusing Standard Oil/Socony nomenclature is flagged rather than silently corrected. The 38 identities introduced by the merged source-wide artifacts were subsequently screened against the complete Scott text; the only new uncited surname lead, Field on page 15, is a common-noun false match.

shortFormReview.method: Initial-free names, corporate base names and generated case-sensitive acronym leads were checked against the actual source passages. Generated acronym candidates were not adopted until identity-resolved. Four further specific roles/information exchanges found; CTIA/CIA, Federation/FBI, US Democratic/Italian Christian Democratic collisions and bibliography-only JCS/NSC were rejected. Additional BCCI pages are conclusion or supporting citations and do not establish new affiliation beyond existing modeled records.
